A production process has 3 sequential stations. 1700 units enter station 1. At each station, a fraction of the units entering are scrapped (removed from the process for good) and another fraction are reworked (repaired at a cost, then continuing on to the next station); the remainder pass with no rework, right first time.

Station 1: scrap rate = 4%, rework rate = 2%, scrap cost = $26/unit scrapped, rework cost = $21/unit reworked
Station 2: scrap rate = 4%, rework rate = 8%, scrap cost = $60/unit scrapped, rework cost = $14/unit reworked
Station 3: scrap rate = 4%, rework rate = 7%, scrap cost = $47/unit scrapped, rework cost = $11/unit reworked

Formulas:
- A station's First-Pass Yield (FPY) = 1 - scrap rate - rework rate (the fraction of units entering that station which pass with no rework at all).
- Units entering the next station = units entering this station x (1 - scrap rate) -- reworked units continue on; only scrapped units leave the process.
- Average FPY = the arithmetic mean of the per-station FPYs.
- Rolled Throughput Yield (RTY) = the product of the per-station FPYs (the fraction of the units entering station 1 that would pass every station right first time, with no rework anywhere).
- Total scrap cost = sum over stations of (units scrapped at that station x that station's scrap cost per unit).
- Total rework cost = sum over stations of (units reworked at that station x that station's rework cost per unit).
- Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ) = Total scrap cost + Total rework cost.

Compute, in this order: (1) Average FPY as a percentage, (2) Rolled Throughput Yield as a percentage, (3) Total scrap cost in dollars, (4) Total rework cost in dollars, (5) COPQ in dollars. Round all values to 2 decimal places.
